newsitem.title: USA: Some upstate NYS cities have problems - official.
newsitem.headline: Some upstate NYS cities have problems - official.

text.p: An official with the New York State comptroller's office on Tuesday said the agency was concerned about the fiscal health of at least a few upstate cities, including Niagara Falls and Schenectady, but added she was not raising red flags.
Patricia Lamb McCarthy, deputy comptroller for municipal affairs in the Office of the State Comptroller, also said that the city of Utica was on the short list of cities that have financial problems.

She explained that this was not a complete list as a number of communities are having difficulties, due to several factors, including cutbacks in state and federal aid, declining tax bases and aging populations.
Further, the lack of timely and accurate information about local communities' finances poses problems for the comptroller's office, which is seeking legislation to reinforce its monitoring role.
"Our bigger fear is that we don't know what's out there," said McCarthy, who spoke at a Bond Buyer Conference on New York Public Finance here.

While Utica this summer avoided having the state impose a Municipal Assistance Corporation (MAC) to oversee its finances and fiscal affairs when it successfully completed a bond sale, the state official noted that this step remans a possibility.

A partnership board that includes elected officials and business leaders was set up to help Utica resolve its problems without a MAC, and the board is helping the city by involving the business community, she said.
